title: Contrast and Readability
summary: Visual contrast is about color relationships and pairing; measurable thresholds are owned by A11Y-002.

MUST.text: Pair foreground and background by lightness difference, not hue alone; verify on real rendered backgrounds.
Provide a scrim or solid backing when text sits on images, gradients or video.
Defer threshold requirements to A11Y-002; this doc covers visual pairing and hierarchy, not numeric pass/fail.

SHOULD.text: Test hover, focus, placeholder, disabled, overlay and dark-mode pairings for visual coherence.
Use distinct contrast between primary, secondary and disabled text tiers (e.g., 100/60/38% opacity on a surface).
Keep borders and dividers visible as structure, not as the only control boundary.

AVOID.text: Pale text for essential information or subtle borders as the only boundary.
Assuming light-mode pairings transfer to dark mode.

DECIDE.decision: Use opacity tier, not a new hue

EXAMPLE.good: "Body text tier 100% opacity, secondary 60%, disabled 38%; scrim behind hero text."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Light gray body on white plus a faint border as the only input edge."

FAILURE_MODES: Visual pairing that looks fine in mockups fails over real image content.
Dark-mode pairs often lose separation between tiers.
Disabled text becomes unreadable or indistinguishable from placeholder.
Borders used as sole boundary disappear in low contrast.
